note: As of 07:02 SGT Fri 20 Nov, pre-Asia-open (SGX/HKEX not yet trading). Thursday 19 Nov was a sharp acceleration of the equity selloff (S&P -2.02%, 4th straight down day; VIX +15.8% to 28.44) alongside another leg down in gold/silver/miners and BTC. Items below are dominated by the Wed 18 Nov evening through Fri 20 Nov morning SGT window; two items (China LPR, Japan CPI) are same-day forward-looking events still pending as of this writeup.

items.headline: Miners crushed harder than metal again -- GDX -3.77%, SILJ -5.66%, SLVP -4.55% vs GLD -1.76%, SLV -2.60% -- as dollar hits fresh 19-month high
items.summary: The US Dollar Index touched 103.97, its highest since April 2025, as Fed officials pushed for a bigger December hike; gold and silver both fell again and the leveraged miner complex (GDX/SILJ/SLVP) amplified the move 2-3x via operating leverage, consistent with Wednesday's pattern. Precious-metals analysts flagged the move as a technically significant break (GDX through its Oct 30 low) and debated whether forced/margin-driven selling was exhausting itself or continuing to build.
items.actionable: This is the single highest-relevance item for the levered silver book: the dollar-strength/hawkish-Fed driver that pushed the loan to -4.2% from a margin call on Wednesday did not reverse Thursday and instead intensified, so treat the margin buffer as still shrinking into Friday's Asia open rather than stabilizing.

items.headline: Fed's Waller renews push for a 50bp December hike ('shock therapy'); Goolsbee says 'all options on the table'; Williams and Daly push back against a jumbo move
items.summary: Governor Christopher Waller reiterated on Thursday that the Fed should consider a half-point hike in December unless officials clearly signal a follow-up January move, warning inflation is 'spreading' and that shock therapy may be necessary. Chicago Fed's Goolsbee said he won't rule out a larger-than-usual increase given 'multiple months of borderline disturbingly high inflation,' while NY Fed's Williams (Nov 17) and SF Fed's Daly (Nov 18) both argued against dramatic/abrupt action, underscoring a genuinely divided FOMC heading into the Dec 8-9 meeting.
items.actionable: Market pricing of a ~95-97% December hike is no longer just a baseline case -- a sitting Fed governor is now explicitly advocating for a larger 50bp move, which is the single biggest tail risk to the silver/gold book if it gains support among other voters before Dec 9.

items.headline: Anthropic's record $81bn Nasdaq IPO pops 17% to close, but euphoria fades into a broad AI-stock selloff that drags S&P to a 4th straight losing day
items.summary: Anthropic (ANT) priced at $83, opened at $111.50 (+34%) and closed at $97.17 (+17%), valuing the company near $1.76 trillion in the largest IPO on record. The initial lift faded by afternoon as megacap AI names reversed hard (Nvidia -3.3%, Alphabet -3.46%, Amazon -3.87%), with the VIX jumping 15.8% to 28.44 (highest since March) as the S&P fell 2.02% for a fourth consecutive loss (Mon -1.92%, Tue -1.03%, Wed -0.23%, Thu -2.02%).
items.actionable: The selloff is now explicitly framed as 'is the AI boom's valuation sustainable' doubt rather than pure rate fear -- a second, distinct risk-off driver layering on top of the hawkish-Fed/dollar story, which raises the odds of continued broad de-risking (including further margin pressure on the leveraged positions) into next week.

items.headline: Tencent slides further (-6.71% Thursday) as AI-capex worries deepen; Hang Seng hits a 4-month low, Hang Seng Tech a 26-month low
items.summary: Tencent fell as much as 6.71% Thursday, a much sharper reaction than Wednesday's initial -0.85% print-day move, as investors kept digesting the 257% capex surge and negative free cash flow from Tuesday's Q3 results. The slide dragged the Hang Seng Index down 1.95% to 22,841.62 (a 4-month low) and the Hang Seng Tech Index down 2.33% to a 26-month low, with US-China tech tensions and new chip-related export restrictions cited as compounding factors.
items.actionable: The capex/FCF-negative thesis flagged Wednesday as 'self-inflicted, not demand weakness' is now driving a materially larger two-day drawdown than initially priced -- re-check position sizing on 0700.HK against the possibility this becomes a multi-day de-rating rather than a one-day dip.

items.headline: New US AI-chip export rule naming Singapore takes effect -- data centers now need a US license, closing a China-access loophole
items.summary: A US Commerce Department interim final rule took effect Thursday Nov 19 requiring data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to obtain a US government license before receiving, re-exporting or transferring advanced AI chips, aimed at preventing Chinese entities (including Huawei and SMIC) from circumventing chip controls via remote compute in third countries. Singapore's government said it is 'studying' the measure and engaging affected companies; Malaysia said it will not negotiate and expects operators to comply.
items.actionable: This directly touches Singapore's data-center/AI-infrastructure ecosystem and reinforces the SMIC chip-control overhang simultaneously -- watch for Singapore-specific compliance costs or data-center capex delays as a second-order drag on the SGX book beyond generic risk-off beta.

items.headline: MP Materials and Lynas extend 3-day winning streaks, bucking the broader selloff on US-China rare-earth-talks optimism
items.summary: MP Materials (+1.98%) and Lynas (+3.40%) both logged a third straight up day Thursday even as the broader market and precious-metals complex sold off hard, with traders positioning around the Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen summit's rare-earth agenda. The move builds on this week's Needham reinstatement of MP at Buy ($48 PT) and reports that MP has cleared a GM magnet-qualification milestone while targeting Apple as a 2027 customer.
items.actionable: Rare earths are now the one portfolio sleeve decoupling positively from the broader risk-off/dollar-strength wave hitting silver, gold miners, crypto and HK tech -- the three-day streak plus concrete GM/Apple offtake progress makes this the strongest 'things are going right' pocket in the book right now.

items.headline: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral in Shenzhen issues a 'peace declaration' and pledges more oil supply, but dodges Ukraine/Iran and leaves rare-earth compliance unresolved
items.summary: The unprecedented three-way summit produced a joint 'peace declaration' committing to strategic stability and UN reform, and a pledge to boost global production/supply of refined petroleum, but made no mention of Ukraine or Iran and announced no concrete new trade breakthroughs. Separately, US officials reiterated that China has delivered only about two-thirds of its Busan rare-earth pledge even as the broader export-curb truce has been extended to Jan 10, 2027 to allow further negotiation.
items.actionable: No concrete new rare-earth or chip-export agreement emerged from the summit itself -- the compliance gap (two-thirds delivered) keeps the China-supply-risk thesis underpinning the rare-earth watchlist intact, while the lack of HK-tech-specific resolution means that sleeve stays exposed to headline risk through the Jan 10 truce deadline.

items.headline: Bitcoin slides to ~$62,154 as November spot-ETF outflows reach roughly $2.6bn cumulative
items.summary: Bitcoin fell further Thursday, tracking the same hawkish-Fed/strong-dollar pressure hitting gold and miners, with US spot BTC ETFs recording cumulative net outflows of about $2.6 billion for the month. Analysts flagged $62,000 as the key support level to watch, warning that a sustained break below it could open a path toward $60,000.
items.actionable: BTC continues to trade as a high-beta, rate-sensitive risk asset in lockstep with gold/miners rather than an uncorrelated hedge -- its ongoing weakness is confirming, not adding new information to, the dominant dollar-strength/hawkish-Fed cross-asset driver already stressing the silver book.

items.headline: China's PBoC due to set November LPR at HK market open -- 23 of 28 economists expect an 18th straight month on hold
items.summary: China's one-year and five-year Loan Prime Rates are due at 01:15 GMT Friday (09:15 SGT), right around the HKEX open. A Reuters poll of 28 economists found 23 (82%) expect both rates held at 3.00%/3.50% for an 18th consecutive month, with the PBoC's shift toward overnight reverse repos as its main policy tool further reducing the LPR's signaling role.
items.actionable: A widely-expected hold means no fresh PBoC stimulus tailwind to offset Thursday's HK-tech selloff at Friday's open -- any surprise cut would be a genuine positive catalyst for 0700.HK/0981.HK/1810.HK, but base case is a non-event.

items.headline: Japan's October core CPI (due later Friday) forecast to accelerate to 2.3%, reinforcing BoJ Governor Ueda's hawkish guidance
items.summary: Japan's national CPI for October is due at 23:30 GMT Friday, with core inflation (ex-fresh food) forecast to rise to 2.3% from 2.1% in September. BoJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Nov 18 the central bank should continue raising rates while anchoring inflation near the 2% target, and markets now price an 82-84% chance of a hike to 1.50% at the Dec 17-18 meeting following firmer producer-price data.
items.actionable: A hawkish BoJ alongside a hawkish Fed is a double dollar-strength/yield-pressure setup for precious metals -- if tonight's CPI beats the 2.3% forecast, expect it to reinforce rather than offset the DXY-strength story that is the dominant threat to the margin-stressed silver position.

items.headline: STI opens down 1.04% as global risk-off spreads to Singapore; S-REITs keep lagging the index
items.summary: The Straits Times Index opened 1.04% lower Thursday amid broad-based declines tracking the global selloff. Singapore REITs continued underperforming, with the FTSE ST All-Share Real Estate REITs Index down 1.56% Wednesday versus the STI's 1.06% decline, extending a year-to-date gap (S-REITs roughly -14% YTD vs STI +12.3%).
items.actionable: The STI weakness is beta to the global risk-off wave rather than a Singapore-specific shock, but the S-REIT underperformance gap is widening again even as the SORA-easing tailwind flagged Monday remains structurally intact -- the REIT sleeve's recovery case is a 2027 story, not a this-week one.

items.headline: Oil holds roughly flat near $83 WTI even as the Shenzhen trilateral pledges more refined-petroleum supply
items.summary: WTI traded little-changed around $83 a barrel Thursday (little moved from Wednesday's API-driven selloff) even after the Trump-Xi-Putin declaration included a joint pledge to 'boost the production and supply' of refined petroleum. No portfolio holding is directly exposed, but a credible supply-side pledge is a mild disinflationary data point working against the hawkish-Fed narrative if it materializes.
items.actionable: Not a direct holding, but worth tracking as a secondary input into the Fed's inflation read -- a genuine supply boost would be a small offset to the Waller/Goolsbee hawkish case that is currently the bigger threat to the silver book.

items.headline: Xiaomi gets a fresh CICC Buy rating ahead of Nov 24 earnings, even as CLSA trims 2026 profit forecast 13% on soft consumer spending
items.summary: Xiaomi is holding up as a relative outperformer within the HK-tech sleeve heading into its Nov 24 Q3 report, with CICC reinstating a Buy rating even as CLSA cut its 2026 adjusted net-profit forecast by 13% citing weaker-than-expected Chinese consumer spending. The stock has continued to tick higher on the rating news despite the broader Tencent-led tech rout.
items.actionable: Xiaomi's relative resilience versus Tencent/SMIC this week suggests the market is still discriminating on fundamentals rather than selling HK tech as one undifferentiated basket -- useful context ahead of the Nov 24 print, which is now the next binary catalyst for the 1810.HK position.
